accepted_gaps.title: A single decisive realization criterion is absent
accepted_gaps.description: Candidate devices are often discussed through isolated signatures, whereas the computational claim spans phase identification, nonlocality, non-Abelian operation, and protected logical behavior.

accepted_gaps.title: Local Majorana-like signatures can be non-diagnostic
accepted_gaps.description: A local spectral or conductance feature can be necessary or suggestive without excluding trivial Andreev-bound-state mechanisms.

accepted_gaps.title: Evidence of non-Abelian manipulation is not yet automatically an engineering proof
accepted_gaps.description: Even a favorable fusion or braid signature must be linked to controls, nonlocal readout, operation fidelity, poisoning exposure, and error scaling before it supports an encoded-computing claim.

accepted_gaps.title: Protection-to-universality bridge is under-specified
accepted_gaps.description: Ising/Majorana topological operations natively supply a protected Clifford subset; a credible architecture needs an explicit, auditable route to non-Clifford resources.

accepted_gaps.title: Cross-device reproducibility and falsification controls need first-class status
accepted_gaps.description: Platform claims should be evaluated against intentionally trivial, scrambled, and held-out device/network conditions rather than favorable traces alone.

rejected_or_deferred.claim: A public announcement of a Majorana breakthrough proves a topological computer exists.
rejected_or_deferred.reason: No announcement is treated as proof without a primary, independently scrutinized experimental record and the multi-axis criteria above.

rejected_or_deferred.claim: Topology removes the need for cooling or error correction.
rejected_or_deferred.reason: Contradicted by the scope of topological protection and by platform engineering requirements.
